item.title: Human-AI collaboration: Opportunities, challenges, and Interdisciplinary Reflections
item.content:encoded:
This special issue explores the multifaceted dimensions of human-AI collaboration, examining both the opportunities it presents and the challenges it raises across various domains and disciplines. The collection seeks interdisciplinary perspectives on how humans and artificial intelligence systems can work together effectively and responsibly.

item.title: Scenario Planning and Foresight: new challenges, emerging practices, and evolving frontiers
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines scenario planning and foresight as evolving methodologies for anticipating and preparing for future challenges. It addresses contemporary developments in how organizations and societies understand and engage with uncertainty, technological change, and strategic planning.

item.title: Sustainable and human-centric management in the era of polycrisis
item.content:encoded:
This special issue for Technology in Society seeks submissions on sustainable and human-centric management approaches in the context of contemporary global crises. The call invites research that addresses how organizations and management practices can balance technological advancement with human values and environmental sustainability.

item.title: The Hidden Costs of Technological Progress: Risks, Governance, and Sustainability in the Transition from Industry 4.0 to Industry 5.0
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines the often-overlooked negative externalities and challenges accompanying technological progress, particularly in the shift toward Industry 5.0. Rather than celebrating innovation uncritically, the call invites research that interrogates the hidden risks, governance gaps, and sustainability concerns that emerge during major industrial transitions.

The special issue seeks contributions that address how societies can navigate technological change while minimizing harm, establishing effective governance mechanisms, and ensuring sustainable outcomes. It welcomes interdisciplinary perspectives on the complex relationship between technological advancement, environmental protection, social welfare, and economic viability.

Appel publié par Technology in Society. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Risks associated with technological advancement and digital transformation
  • Governance frameworks for emerging technologies
  • Sustainability implications of Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0
  • Environmental and social costs of technological progress
  • Policy and regulatory approaches to managing technological transitions
  • Ethical considerations in technology deployment
  • Human and organizational impacts of industrial transformation

Timeline

  • January 18, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Artificial Intelligence, Business, and Epochal Change
item.content:encoded:
Glen Whelan, ESG UQÀM

Gabriel Weber, ESSCA School of Management

Yann Truong, ESSCA School of Management

Ongoing developments in Artificial Intelligence (AI) indicate that machine learning technologies will not simply match, but will potentially significantly surpass, a wide range of human cognitive abilities. Given this trend, there is reason to believe that AI could threaten humanity's hegemonic, agentic, positioning and that it could be a driver of civilizational, epochal change.

Business actors occupy a unique dual-position within this context. First, as leading architects of AI development, high-tech corporations are rebuilding the organizational structures, labour markets, and human-machinic assemblages that will define social existence for decades to come by impacting upon such fundamental concerns as democracy, peace, and human flourishing. Second, the institution of business and markets as a whole will also find itself the subject of transformative forces that it cannot control despite the fact that certain actors therewithin – such as high-tech corporations – have given rise to them.

Appel publié par Business & Society. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Speed versus safety in the rush to develop (super-intelligent) AI
  • Competition and conflict over AI resources
  • Defense, offense, and critical AI infrastructure
  • (Rogue) AI and principal-agent misalignment
  • AI and 'responsibility gaps'
  • Existential threats and AI
  • AI and the implicit/explicit embodiment of political goals and values
  • Corporate elites (e.g., owners/founders) and the control of AI
  • Corporate governance within the AI political context
  • Ideological conflict in the era of AI
  • The algocratic and epistocratic underpinnings of AI developments
  • AI and planetary boundaries
  • Environmental justice and AI

  • Resource creation, extraction and commodification in the era of AI
  • AI and exosomatic energy use
  • AI and the changing value of human labour and human leisure
  • The possibility of human excellence and flourishing in AI impacted societies

  • The implications of AI for how we conceive and value human rights, democracy and justice
